verdict.rationale: BigQuery's pricing page documents two compute models: on-demand per-TiB scanned with the first 1 TiB free, and reserved slots billed as virtual-CPU capacity over time. A free tier of 10 GiB storage and 1 TiB of queries is also published. Community users confirm the console shows bytes to be scanned before a query runs, which can be multiplied by the $6.25/TB rate to get the cost. However, others report that the bytes-scanned and slots units are hard to translate into dollars ahead of time, and one user received a $14k surprise bill from a scripted workload, so monthly estimation is achievable but not straightforward. Missing for 10: storage pricing rates beyond the free tier, any documented pricing calculator or dollar-denominated estimate, and clear guidance for projecting slot-based or scripted workloads to a monthly figure.
